notes: About 92 % for ordinary glass; coatings raise it above 99 %.

name: Ideal Anti-Reflection Coating Index
description: Gives the refractive index a single quarter-wave coating needs to cancel reflection completely at its design wavelength.
notes: For glass that is 1.23; MgF₂ (1.38) is the usual compromise.

name: Quarter-Wave Coating Reflectance
description: Gives the reflectance at the design wavelength of glass with a single quarter-wave anti-reflection layer.
notes: MgF₂ on crown glass cuts reflection from about 4.3 % to about 1.3 %.

name: Coefficient of Finesse
description: Gives the coefficient of finesse F of a Fabry–Pérot cavity, which sets how sharp its transmission peaks are.
notes: Not the same as the finesse ℱ = π√F / 2.

name: Fabry–Pérot Transmission (Airy Function)
description: Gives the fraction of light transmitted by a lossless Fabry–Pérot etalon at round-trip phase δ = 4πnd cos θ/λ.
notes: Full transmission when δ is a multiple of 2π.

name: Single-Slit Diffraction Intensity
expression: i0 * (sin(pi * a * sin(rad(th)) / lm) / (pi * a * sin(rad(th)) / lm))^2
description: Gives the intensity of the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern of a single slit at angle θ: I₀(sin β/β)².
notes: Zero at a sin θ = mλ; side lobes are 4.5 %, 1.6 %, … of the centre.

name: Double-Slit Intensity with Diffraction Envelope
expression: i0 * cos(pi * d * sin(rad(th)) / lm)^2 * (sin(pi * a * sin(rad(th)) / lm) / (pi * a * sin(rad(th)) / lm))^2
description: Gives the intensity of Young's double-slit pattern including the single-slit envelope.
notes: Interference fringes that land on envelope zeros are missing orders.

name: Multi-Slit Grating Intensity
expression: i0 * (sin(nn * pi * d * sin(rad(th)) / lm) / (nn * sin(pi * d * sin(rad(th)) / lm)))^2
description: Gives the interference intensity of N equally spaced narrow slits, normalised to 1 at the principal maxima.
notes: More slits make the main peaks sharper, with N − 2 small peaks between them.

name: Airy Pattern Intensity (Circular Aperture)
expression: i0 * (2 * besselj(1, pi * dd * sin(rad(th)) / lm) / (pi * dd * sin(rad(th)) / lm))^2
description: Gives the Fraunhofer diffraction intensity of a circular aperture, I₀(2J₁(x)/x)² with x = πD sin θ/λ (Airy 1835).
notes: The first dark ring is at sin θ = 1.22 λ/D.

name: Gaussian Beam Wavefront Radius of Curvature
description: Gives the curvature radius of a Gaussian laser beam's wavefront at distance z; it is smallest (2z_R) at z = z_R.
notes: Flat (infinite) at the waist and like a spherical wave far away.

name: Gouy Phase of a Gaussian Beam
description: Gives the extra phase a focused beam picks up relative to a plane wave; π in total through a focus (Gouy 1890).
notes: Sets the mode spacing of laser cavities.

name: Beam Parameter Product
description: Gives the beam parameter product, a measure of beam quality that no lens can improve; λ/π for a perfect Gaussian beam.
notes: Fibre lasers are specified by BPP; divide by λ/π for M².

name: Lateral Shift through a Glass Plate
expression: t * sin(rad(ti) - asin(sin(rad(ti)) / n)) / cos(asin(sin(rad(ti)) / n))
description: Gives the sideways displacement of a ray passing through a flat parallel plate; the ray leaves parallel to its original direction.
notes: Used for image shifting in microscopes and cameras.

name: Primary Rainbow Angle
description: Gives the angle between the antisolar point and the primary rainbow from the minimum deviation of light reflected once inside a droplet (Descartes 1637).
notes: Red (n ≈ 1.331) is at about 42.4°, violet (n ≈ 1.343) at about 40.6°.

name: Luminous Flux from Radiant Power
description: Converts optical power at one wavelength into lumens: 683 lm/W times the eye's sensitivity V(λ), 1 at 555 nm.
notes: Red 650 nm light has V ≈ 0.107, so 1 W gives only about 73 lm.

name: Luminance of a Matte (Lambertian) Surface
description: Gives the brightness of an ideally diffuse surface lit with a given illuminance: L = ρE/π.
notes: White paper under 500 lx office lighting is about 127 cd/m².

name: Lumens of an Isotropic Source from Candela
description: Gives the total luminous flux of a source that shines equally in every direction.
notes: For a beam, use 2π(1 − cos(half-angle)) instead of 4π.

name: Lumens in a Beam from Candela and Beam Angle
description: Estimates the luminous flux in a spotlight beam from its centre intensity and beam angle, assuming uniform intensity inside the cone.
notes: Real beams fall off towards the edge, so this is an upper estimate.

name: A-Weighting Correction
description: Gives the A-weighting correction at a frequency (IEC 61672), approximating the ear's lower sensitivity to low and very high sounds.
notes: About −19.1 dB at 100 Hz, 0 dB at 1 kHz.

name: Sound Level of N Identical Sources
description: Gives the combined level of N equal, incoherent sources: each doubling adds about 3 dB.
notes: Ten identical machines are 10 dB louder than one.

name: Equivalent Continuous Sound Level (Leq)
description: Gives the steady level with the same total sound energy as a varying one, averaged over equal intervals.
notes: Loud moments dominate: one 80 dB interval outweighs several at 65–70 dB.

name: Daily Noise Exposure Level (LEX,8h)
description: Normalises a noise exposure to an 8-hour working day (ISO 9612), for comparison with workplace limits such as 85 dB(A).
notes: Halving the time lowers the daily level by 3 dB.

name: Permissible Noise Exposure Time (NIOSH)
description: Gives the daily time allowed at a given level under the NIOSH recommendation: 8 h at 85 dB(A), halved for every 3 dB more.
notes: At 100 dB(A) only 15 minutes.

name: Noise Dose
description: Adds up the fractions of allowed exposure time spent at each level (NIOSH, 3 dB exchange rate); over 100 % exceeds the limit.

name: Closed Pipe Resonance with End Correction
description: Gives the resonances of a pipe closed at one end (odd harmonics only), with the 0.6 r end correction at the open end.
notes: Used in the resonance-tube method to measure the speed of sound.

name: Ultrasound Attenuation in Soft Tissue
description: Gives the round-trip loss of an ultrasound echo from depth d, about 0.5 dB per cm per MHz in soft tissue.
notes: Why deep imaging needs lower frequencies (and lower resolution).

name: Sound Absorption Coefficient from Impedance Tube
description: Gives a material's normal-incidence absorption coefficient from the standing-wave ratio measured in an impedance tube (ISO 10534-1).
notes: SWR = 1 means perfect absorption.

name: Noise Reduction between Rooms
description: Gives the level difference between two rooms from the partition's transmission loss, its area and the receiving room's absorption.
notes: A larger shared wall or a more echoey receiving room lets more sound through.

name: Capillary Wave Speed
description: Gives the speed of ripples short enough to be driven by surface tension rather than gravity.
notes: Below about 1.7 cm on water, shorter ripples travel faster.

name: Wave Intensity from Amplitude (Sinusoid in a Medium)
description: Gives the intensity of a sinusoidal wave from the medium's density and wave speed and the displacement amplitude.
notes: A 1 kHz sound with 10 nm displacement amplitude is about 81 dB.

name: Etalon Resolving Power
expression: pi * sqrt(r) / (1 - r) * 2 * nn * d / lm
description: Gives λ/Δλ for a Fabry–Pérot etalon: finesse times interference order.
notes: Millions are easy — far beyond a prism or a grating.

name: Prism Resolving Power
description: Gives the resolving power λ/Δλ of a prism filled by the beam: base length times the glass's dispersion.
notes: A 5 cm flint-glass prism can just split the sodium D lines (resolving power about 1000).

name: Depth of Focus of an Optical System
description: Gives the axial range over which a microscope or lithography image stays sharp; it shrinks with the square of the numerical aperture.
notes: Why high-NA lithography needs very flat wafers.

name: Lithography Resolution (Rayleigh)
description: Gives the smallest printable half-pitch of a photolithography system.
notes: EUV (13.5 nm) with NA 0.33 and k₁ 0.4 reaches about 16 nm.
